titulo: Prueba de Acceso a la Universidad 2027 — Lengua Extranjera II: Inglés — Aragón
instrucciones: This exam consists of 6 exercises divided into 3 parts. Answer all the exercises in English. The marks assigned to each exercise are shown in brackets. Exercises 1 and 2 are based on the text in Exercise 1. In Exercise 1.1, write True or False and justify each answer with a direct quotation from the text. In Exercise 1.2, answer THREE of the FOUR questions in your own words. In Exercise 2.1, find words or phrases in the text with the meanings given. In Exercise 2.2 and Exercise 2.3, answer only the number of items requested; if you answer more, only the first requested answers will be corrected. In Exercise 3, choose ONE writing task and write 100–120 words in English.

preguntas.enunciado:
PART 1. READING COMPREHENSION. Read the text and answer Exercise 1.1. (1.5 points)

BORROWING INSTEAD OF BUYING: A NEIGHBOURHOOD LIBRARY OF THINGS

When Aisha Rahman moved to Riverside, a district of York, in 2021, she noticed that people often bought equipment they used only once or twice. A camping stove, a sewing machine or a power drill could be expensive, and many residents had nowhere to store them. Aisha and four neighbours decided to try a different approach. They set up Borrow Better, a community-run library where members can borrow useful objects rather than buy them.

The project began in a room at a local community centre. It now operates from a small unit near the bus station and has a collection of around 200 items, including tools, kitchen equipment and board games. Residents can join for £18 a year, while people who cannot afford the fee can request a free membership. Members check the online catalogue and reserve an item through the website or by phone. They usually collect it from the unit and can keep it for seven days. If nobody else has reserved it, they may renew the loan once.

Before an item goes out, a trained volunteer checks that it is clean and in working order. Borrow Better also holds a repair workshop every three months, where volunteers show residents how to mend simple household objects. The workshop is separate from the lending service: it does not offer professional repairs.

During its first year, the project recorded 1,200 loans and attracted 430 members. In a survey, 68% of respondents said they had borrowed something they would otherwise have bought. The organisers believe this can reduce unnecessary purchases, but they are careful about making claims. They have not measured the project’s carbon savings directly; their estimate is based on members’ survey answers.

The project has also faced practical difficulties. Its collection is growing, but storage space is limited, and some borrowers return items late. Volunteers now send reminder emails before the due date. A small grant from the local council has helped Borrow Better open a second collection point at a youth centre. Aisha hopes that the project will make sharing ordinary and convenient, while giving neighbours more opportunities to meet and help one another.

1.1. Add True or False and justify each answer with a direct quotation from the text. A correct answer with its correct justification is worth 0.5 points. (3 items)
1.1.1. Borrow Better was originally created by the local council.
1.1.2. Members can reserve objects online or by phone.
1.1.3. The organisers have directly measured the carbon savings produced by the project.
preguntas.solucion:
### 1.1.1
**False.** Borrow Better was started by Aisha and four neighbours, not by the local council. The text says: “Aisha and four neighbours decided to try a different approach. They set up Borrow Better, a community-run library where members can borrow useful objects rather than buy them.”

### 1.1.2
**True.** Members can reserve objects using either of the stated methods. The text says: “Members check the online catalogue and reserve an item through the website or by phone.”

### 1.1.3
**False.** The organisers have not directly measured the carbon savings. The text says: “They have not measured the project’s carbon savings directly; their estimate is based on members’ survey answers.”
preguntas.criterios: 0,5 puntos por cada uno de los tres apartados (1,5 puntos en total). En cada apartado, 0,25 puntos por indicar correctamente True/False y 0,25 puntos por justificarlo con una cita directa pertinente y fiel al texto. Se acepta la convención numérica True = 1 y False = 0.

1.2.2. What does a member need to do to borrow an object, and how long can they normally keep it?

preguntas.enunciado:
2.2. Complete TWO of the following sentences by choosing the correct option (a, b, c or d). Each answer is worth 0.25 points. If you answer more than two, only your first two answers will be corrected.
2.2.1. If an item ___ available, members can reserve it online.
a) is   b) will be   c) was   d) has
2.2.2. Members ___ return borrowed objects within seven days, unless they renew the loan.
a) must   b) might   c) would   d) could
2.2.3. Neither the drill nor the sewing machine ___ available for collection on Tuesday.
a) are   b) is   c) have   d) were
2.2.4. The new collection point, ___ opened last month, is inside the youth centre.
a) who   b) where   c) which   d) whose
preguntas.solucion:
### Método: comprobar la función gramatical del espacio en blanco

Respondo solo las dos primeras, como indica el enunciado.

1. **2.2.1.** En la cláusula condicional introducida por *if*, se usa el presente simple para expresar una condición posible: *If an item **is** available...* La opción **a) is** concuerda con el sujeto singular *an item*. Se descartan *will be*, *was* y *has* porque no forman aquí la construcción requerida.

2. **2.2.2.** El espacio requiere un verbo modal que exprese obligación: los miembros **deben** devolver los objetos prestados en siete días. La opción **a) must** expresa esa obligación; *might*, *would* y *could* no la expresan en este contexto.

**Comprobación:** las frases completas quedan: *If an item is available, members can reserve it online* y *Members must return borrowed objects within seven days, unless they renew the loan.* Ambas son gramaticales y coherentes con el significado.
preguntas.criterios: 0,25 puntos por cada opción correcta entre las dos respondidas; 0 puntos por cada opción incorrecta. Máximo: 0,50 puntos. Según el enunciado, solo se corrigen las dos primeras respuestas si se contestan más de dos.

preguntas.enunciado:
2.3. Complete TWO of the following sentences so that they mean the same as the sentence before them. Use the word in capitals without changing it. Each answer is worth 0.3 points. If you answer more than two, only your first two answers will be corrected.
2.3.1. Volunteers check every object before lending it. (IS)
Every object ___ before it is lent.
2.3.2. Borrow Better began lending objects in 2021. (BEEN)
Borrow Better ___ objects since 2021.
2.3.3. The membership fee is so low that many families can afford it. (SUCH)
It is ___ that many families can afford it.
2.3.4. You can renew the loan if nobody else has reserved the object. (UNLESS)
You can renew the loan ___ the object has been reserved by somebody else.
preguntas.solucion:
### Respuestas elegidas: 2.3.1 y 2.3.2

**2.3.1.** *Every object **is checked** before it is lent.*

1. La oración original está en presente simple y tiene como objeto directo *every object*.
2. Al pasarla a voz pasiva, ese objeto pasa a ser el sujeto; se usa *is* y el participio pasado *checked*.
3. Se conserva la expresión *before it is lent*.

**2.3.2.** *Borrow Better **has been lending** objects since 2021.*

1. *Since 2021* indica que la actividad comenzó en el pasado y continúa en el presente.
2. Para expresar una actividad continuada se usa el presente perfecto continuo: *has been* + verbo en *-ing*.
3. El sujeto singular *Borrow Better* requiere *has*. Se conserva la palabra dada, *BEEN*, sin modificarla.

**Comprobación:** *is checked* mantiene el sentido de la pasiva de la primera oración; *has been lending ... since 2021* expresa que los préstamos comenzaron en 2021 y siguen teniendo lugar.
preguntas.criterios: 0,3 puntos por cada transformación correcta: 2.3.1 exige “is checked” y la conservación del sentido y del resto de la oración; 2.3.2 exige “has been lending” con “since 2021”. Total: 0,6 puntos. Según el enunciado, si se contestan más de dos apartados, solo se corrigen los dos primeros.

preguntas.enunciado:
PART 3. WRITING. Choose ONE of the following tasks and write 100–120 words in English. (4 points)
A. Your school newsletter is planning a feature on practical ways to make the local community more sustainable. Write an email to the editor suggesting a scheme for sharing useful objects in your area. Explain what people could share, how the scheme could work and what benefits or challenges it might have.
B. Write an opinion piece for a youth website answering this question: Should local councils invest more in shared community spaces and services instead of encouraging people to buy more things? Give reasons and include a relevant example.
preguntas.solucion:
### Opción elegida: A

**Paso 1.** Se incluyen los tres elementos solicitados: qué objetos compartir, cómo organizar el sistema y qué ventajas y dificultades tendría.

**Paso 2.** Se emplea el formato de correo, con saludo, tono apropiado y despedida.

**Paso 3. Modelo de respuesta (108 palabras en el cuerpo; 118 contando asunto, saludo y despedida):**

**Subject: A neighbourhood sharing library**

Dear Editor,

I would like to suggest creating a neighbourhood sharing library for useful objects. Residents could lend tools, camping equipment, board games and kitchen appliances that they only use occasionally. A simple website or noticeboard at the community centre could list each item, its owner and availability. Members would book items, collect them, and return them by an agreed date; a small deposit could cover damage.

This scheme would save families money and reduce waste because fewer new products would be needed. It could also help neighbours meet and support one another. However, items might be damaged or returned late, so clear rules and volunteer coordinators would be important.

Yours sincerely,
Alex

**Corrección propuesta:** 4/4 puntos. La respuesta se ajusta a la extensión, desarrolla todos los aspectos de la tarea y mantiene una organización y un registro adecuados.
preguntas.resultado: Opción A: correo de 108 palabras en el cuerpo (118 con asunto, saludo y despedida); puntuación propuesta: 4/4.
preguntas.criterios: Reparto orientativo sobre 4 puntos: cumplimiento de la tarea y desarrollo de las ideas, 1 punto; organización, cohesión y adecuación al formato y registro, 1 punto; vocabulario y variedad léxica, 1 punto; corrección gramatical, ortográfica y de puntuación, 1 punto. Se puede descontar proporcionalmente si no se respeta la extensión o se omiten elementos importantes.
